name: cli-init
body: `kalide init [path]` in the current directory creates the deck's `slides/`, an empty `assets/` directory for images, and a valid `kalide.yaml`. With no argument it writes one valid starter slide into `slides/` and also creates the project's minimal local `templates/` directory (see cli-init-minimal-seed), and refuses if a local `templates/` already exists. When the optional `path` argument is given it names an external template library (see external-template-library): init writes `templates: <path>` into `kalide.yaml`, writes an empty `slides/` (NO starter slide), writes NO local `templates/`, and validates the library at `path` fail-fast BEFORE writing anything — a valid library needs only `library.yaml` plus the templates-dir-layout structure and need not define any template, but the deck's theme (optional, default `default`) must resolve in it (theme-selection); an invalid or missing library, or a library that does not resolve the deck's theme, aborts with a clear error naming the path, a non-zero exit and nothing written. With a path, a pre-existing local `templates/` does not block init (see cli-init-refuse-existing); it is left untouched and ignored. The path is stored as given (a relative path stays relative, resolved against the deck root). AC: immediately after a no-arg init, `kalide start` validates cleanly and serves the starter slide; after `kalide init ../lib` against a library that resolves the deck's theme (which need not define any template), `kalide start` validates and serves the deck from `../lib` (the slide set may be empty); `kalide init ../bad-lib` — invalid library, or a library that does not resolve the deck's theme — fails before writing anything.
